title: Roof Inspections in Mission, TX | Edel Roofing & Construction
description: Free roof inspections in Mission, TX. Find out how much life is left on an original 2000s roof before you buy, sell, or renew insurance. Call (956) 422-3335.
lede: Edel Roofing & Construction inspects roofs on Mission homes and buildings for free. You get a written report with photos and a straight answer about how much life the roof has left.

sections.title: The question most Mission homeowners have
paras: About half of Mission's homes were built in 2000 or later, and the median year built is 2000 (Census ACS 2020 to 2024). Most of those houses still have their first roof, and that roof is now around 20 years old. In Valley heat, that is about where a shingle roof starts to run out of life.

So the question we hear most is simple: how long do I have? Some original roofs still have several good years. Others need work now. You cannot tell from the driveway. An inspection on the roof itself answers it.

sections.title: What we look at on a Mission roof

cards.title: Shingles
cards.body: Granule loss, brittleness, cracks, curling, and hail bruises across every slope, not just the front.

cards.title: Flashing
cards.body: The metal and sealant at walls, chimneys, and valleys, where 20 year old sealant tends to dry out first.

cards.title: Vents and pipe boots
cards.body: Rubber boots crack in the sun and are one of the most common leak points on older roofs.

cards.title: Decking
cards.body: Soft spots under foot that point to a slow leak and rotting wood below the shingles.

cards.title: Gutters and edges
cards.body: Where water leaves the roof, and whether it is backing up under the edge.

cards.title: Attic, if needed
cards.body: Stains, damp insulation, or daylight that show where water is getting in.

sections.title: Storms, rain, and roofs in Mission
paras: Mission roofs have been through a lot in the last decade. Hurricane Hanna dropped 14.40 inches of rain on the city in July 2020. In April 2023, spotters reported hail up to 2.5 inches in Mission. A roof can come through storms like those with damage that does not leak right away. If yours has never been checked since, an inspection gives you a written record of its condition today.

sections.title: Insurance facts for Mission homeowners
paras: Hidalgo County is not in the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association area, which covers 14 coastal counties. So a Mission roof does not need a TDI windstorm certificate for TWIA coverage. Your regular homeowners insurance still cares about the roof. The Texas Department of Insurance says insurers cannot refuse or drop a policy because of roof age alone, but they can look at condition, and some pay older roofs at actual cash value.

About 71% of Mission homes are lived in by their owners. If you are buying one built in the 2000s and the roof was never replaced, plan for a new roof in the next few years, and use a written report when you negotiate.

faqs.q: My house was built in the early 2000s. Is the roof original?
faqs.a: If nobody has replaced it, probably. Roof work is not always in the listing or the seller's disclosure. An inspection shows the roof's condition either way.

faqs.q: How much life does a 20 year old roof have left?
faqs.a: It depends on how it was installed, the ventilation, and the storms it has seen. Some have several good years, some need replacing now. That is what the inspection tells you.

faqs.q: Do I need a windstorm certificate to sell my Mission house?
faqs.a: Not for TWIA. Hidalgo County is outside the TWIA coastal area. Ask your agent or lender if your buyer's insurer has its own requirements.

faqs.q: How long does a roof inspection take?
faqs.a: Most residential roofs take 30 to 45 minutes. You get the written report the same visit.

faqs.q: How do I book an inspection in Mission?
faqs.a: Call (956) 422-3335 or book an inspection online. We come from Edinburg, about 26 minutes away.
